steps.title: ContextOS
steps.subtitle: Shared decisions. Traceable work. | Three-Way Handshake
steps.caption: ContextOS · Hackathon MVP
steps.narration: ContextOS keeps a software team and its AI agents working from the same accepted decisions.

steps.caption: A project overview with clear next actions
steps.narration: Teams see accepted knowledge, pending reviews, affected work, and the next useful action in one workspace.

steps.caption: Synthetic walkthrough · no live model calls in this recording
steps.narration: This public walkthrough uses synthetic data. The separate protected team service has verified live Gemini and shared storage.

steps.caption: 1 · Product intent becomes accepted knowledge
steps.narration: We start with product intent. The requirement has an owner, an identifier, and an accepted revision.

steps.caption: Inspect each checkpoint, one action at a time
steps.narration: Each checkpoint reveals the acting persona and the exact decision available at that moment.

steps.caption: 2 · Architecture uses the same requirement
steps.narration: The architect receives that accepted requirement without relying on someone else’s private conversation.

steps.caption: 3 · Development keeps the original intent
steps.narration: Development works from the same revision, with exact sources that can be inspected.

steps.caption: 4 · QA checks the same contract
steps.narration: QA receives the same requirement, keeping acceptance checks connected to the product decision.

steps.caption: One decision survives the handoff
steps.narration: The requirement survives the handoff across product, architecture, development, and quality.

steps.caption: Publication needs an independent owner
steps.narration: Shared memory also needs governance. A suggestion must never silently become an accepted decision.

steps.caption: Review a proposed architecture change
steps.narration: Here, a developer proposes a change to the retry design.

steps.caption: The proposal starts pending
steps.narration: The proposal records its source and reason, while accepted knowledge remains unchanged.

steps.caption: Self-approval is blocked
steps.narration: The author cannot approve the proposal. The application enforces that boundary before publication.

steps.caption: The architect reviews the exact proposal
steps.narration: An independent architect reviews the exact proposal, including its content hash and accepted base revision.

steps.caption: Publication creates a new revision
steps.narration: Publication creates a new accepted revision and records who made the decision.

steps.caption: Review evidence stays inspectable
steps.narration: The completed walkthrough preserves the decision evidence for inspection.

steps.caption: A changed decision flags affected work
steps.narration: Now change the retry limit. Existing work must know that its source changed.

steps.caption: Keep the original source snapshot
steps.narration: The original run keeps its source snapshot, so its earlier answer remains explainable.

steps.caption: The owner publishes the revised constraint
steps.narration: After independent publication, ContextOS flags the work affected by the changed decision.

steps.caption: Refresh against accepted revision two
steps.narration: QA refreshes against the new revision. The old run remains intact for comparison.

steps.caption: History is preserved, not overwritten
steps.narration: A refresh updates the working context without rewriting the evidence of earlier work.

steps.caption: Security follows the context
steps.narration: Finally, the security case shows that shared knowledge still respects role boundaries.

steps.caption: Security can inspect restricted findings
steps.narration: The security persona can inspect explicitly restricted context within its authorized scope.

steps.caption: Other roles cannot retrieve restricted context
steps.narration: A developer cannot retrieve those restricted findings. Permissions are checked before context assembly.

steps.caption: Derived task output is protected too
steps.narration: The boundary also applies to derived task output, rather than hiding only the original document.

steps.caption: Activity respects the same access boundary
steps.narration: Related activity is filtered too, so the audit view does not leak restricted knowledge.

steps.caption: Five personas · one governed workspace
steps.narration: Every persona can act within its scope, with visible outcomes and clear ownership.

steps.caption: Twelve repeatable cases for judges to explore
steps.narration: The full walkthrough catalog covers conflicts, rollback, rejection, context budgets, attribution, and honest usage reporting.

steps.caption: Verify all twelve cases
steps.narration: Judges can repeat every case, then use a private member login to test the live team workflow.

steps.caption: A working MVP on Google Cloud
steps.narration: The team service runs on Cloud Run with Firestore and live Gemini on Vertex AI.

steps.title: Keep decisions connected to work
steps.subtitle: ContextOS | Three-Way Handshake | Explore the hosted MVP
steps.caption: ContextOS · Shared knowledge with ownership and evidence
steps.narration: ContextOS makes accepted decisions reusable, changes visible, and agent work traceable. Explore the MVP and inspect the evidence.
